source_text: 70. Si le prophète s'écrie ensuite: «Qui racontera sa naissance?» (Is 53, 8) C'est de peur que, témoins de la haine de ses ennemis et des souffrances de sa passion, nous n'arrivions à le mépriser comme un homme vil et abject; c'est pour opérer notre conversion. Celui qui a supporté tout cela possède une génération inénarrable, parce que le prophète appelle génération son origine, c'est-à-dire son Père, qui est inénarrable et indicible. Reconnais donc que telle est précisément l'origine de celui qui a enduré ces souffrances. Ne le méprise donc pas à cause des tourments qu'il a endurés à dessein pour toi; mais crains-le à cause de son origine
pass_a_gloss: §70 dual gloss (Armenian-via-French sense) ≠ Pass B running English. Theme: Unutterable generation = the Father; do not despise the sufferer.
pass_b_english: If the prophet then cries: ‘Who shall declare his generation?’ ([[Isa 53:8 >> Bible:Isa 53:8]]), it is lest, witnessing the hatred of his enemies and the sufferings of his passion, we should come to despise him as a vile and abject human being; it is to work our conversion.

He who has borne all this possesses an unutterable generation, because the prophet calls generation his origin — that is, his Father, who is unutterable and ineffable. ([[Mt 11:27 >> Bible:Mt 11:27]]; [[Jn 1:18 >> Bible:Jn 1:18]]) Recognize, then, that such precisely is the origin of him who endured these sufferings. Do not despise him because of the torments he endured on purpose for you; but fear him because of his origin. ([[Phil 2:6-11 >> Bible:Phil 2:6-11]])
